newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil confirms Israel gas contacts.
newsitem.headline: Statoil confirms Israel gas contacts.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Monday it had been in contact with parties in Israel as part of attempts to revitalise plans to exploit oil and gas reserves at its Snoehvit discovery.
But, it said, no formal negotiations had begun.
The company was responding to media reports that leading Israeli industrialists, Ofer Brothers, had proposed a deal to import natural gas from Norway.

"In the course of reviewing plans for Snoehvit and revaluating marketing opportunities there has been contact (with Israeli parties), but there has not been anything near to negotiations," Statoil spokesman Lars Gunnar Dahle told Reuters.
He declined to name the parties the company had had contacts with.
The Snoehvit prospect lies far north in the Barents Sea within the Arctic Circle and is estimated to hold about 150 billion cubic metres of recoverable gas.
Previous studies for development found the project uneconomical due to its distance from customers and the lack of infrastructure in the area.

In September, Statoil said it had restarted work on a development plan and on a sales solution for liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the fields. It said it saw possible sales opportunities in the Middle East and the U.S. East Coast.
Gas would be produced from subsea wells with new multiphase flow technology allowing the hydrocarbon streams to be piped to land for processing and liquefaction before export by ship.
"There have been several attempts to try and get Snoehvit on track. It's a challenging development both on the technical front and for infrastructure," Dahle said.
Statoil is operator of production licences 110 and 099, while Norsk Hydro ASA operates 097. All three licences embrace Snoehvit.
Other partners are Total, Elf Petroleum, Fina Inc, Amerada Hess and Germany's Deminex.
